skill.name: diagnosing-bugs
skill.description: Guides agents through a disciplined bug diagnosis loop for hard defects and performance regressions, from reproducible feedback loops to cleanup.
skill.summary: Diagnose hard bugs with reproducible loops, ranked hypotheses, targeted instrumentation, regression tests, and cleanup.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Hard bugs waste time when teams guess before proving the failure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reproducible loops, hypotheses, instrumentation, fixes, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Guides the agent to build a tight feedback loop before forming hypotheses.
Supports failing tests, HTTP scripts, CLI fixtures, browser automation, trace replay, and human-in-the-loop prompts.
Requires reproduction and minimization before deeper diagnosis work begins.
Structures debugging around three to five ranked, falsifiable hypotheses.
Promotes targeted instrumentation tied to specific predictions.
Adds cleanup and post-mortem steps after the fix and regression test.
limitations: It depends on access to the project, test environment, or reproduction artifact.
Manual UI bugs may still require a person to perform steps and report results.
It does not replace product context or domain knowledge from maintainers.
It guides diagnosis but cannot guarantee that a correct test seam exists.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Production Bugs
use_cases.description: Create a focused loop from logs, traces, or user reports before changing code.

use_cases.title: Investigate Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Establish a measurement baseline, compare states, and test targeted performance hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Debug Reviews
use_cases.description: Use a shared diagnosis process so reviewers can see the repro, hypothesis, fix, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Start Bug Diagnosis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured debugging pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this bug using the diagnosing-bugs skill. First build a tight reproduction loop, then show me the result before proposing fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Minimize a Reproduction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after a failure has been reproduced.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs process to reduce this repro to the smallest scenario that still fails. Explain what remains load-bearing.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Debug Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when the failure is known but the cause is unclear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three to five ranked hypotheses for this bug. For each one, state a prediction and the next probe that would falsify it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Performance Regression
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for slow behavior after a change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this performance regression. Build a baseline measurement, compare the changed state, instrument only targeted boundaries, and propose a regression test.

output_examples.input: A checkout flow sometimes saves duplicate orders after payment.
output: A reproduction loop that exercises the payment callback and checks for one order.
A minimized scenario showing the duplicate appears only when retry headers are present.
Ranked hypotheses covering idempotency, transaction boundaries, and callback retries.
A fix plan with a regression test at the callback boundary.

output_examples.input: A dashboard became slower after a recent release.
output: A baseline timing measurement for the slow view before code changes.
A comparison between the previous and current release paths.
Targeted probes around query count, rendering cost, and data transformation time.
A cleanup checklist that removes temporary instrumentation.

output_examples.input: A UI export button fails only in a browser session.
output: A human-in-the-loop script that asks the user to perform the browser action.
Captured answers that record whether the error appeared and what message was shown.
A follow-up plan to replace manual steps with automation when possible.

best_practices: Build a red-capable loop before reading code for a theory.
Change one variable at a time when testing a hypothesis.
Remove temporary logs and throwaway harnesses before declaring the fix complete.
anti_patterns: Do not start with a single favorite hypothesis before a repro exists.
Do not log everything and search the noise later.
Do not add a shallow regression test that misses the real failure path.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents diagnose hard bugs and performance regressions through reproduction, minimization, hypotheses, instrumentation, fixes, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the debugging workflow. Code changes happen only after the reproduction and hypothesis work support a specific fix.

faq.question: Can it handle flaky bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to raise the reproduction rate and make the signal deterministic enough for debugging.

faq.question: When should I use the human-in-the-loop script?
faq.answer: Use it when a person must click through a UI or provide observed results that automation cannot capture yet.

faq.question: How does it address performance regressions?
faq.answer: It starts with baseline measurements, then compares states and uses targeted probes instead of broad logging.

faq.question: What should the final result include?
faq.answer: The final result should include a fixed original repro, a passing regression test or noted test gap, and removed debug instrumentation.
